newsitem.title: USA: USDA research under review for bias to big farms.
newsitem.headline: USDA research under review for bias to big farms.

text.p: The National Academy of Sciences will review Agriculture Department research programs to see if they are biased against small and medium size farmers, Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said on Wednesday.
"This independent review ... will help ensure that these farmers benefit from the wide variety of research conducted by USDA," Glickman said in a statement.

During a news conference, Catherine Woteki, acting undersecretary for research, said examinations by USDA found its research was "scale-neutral" and useful to all farmers. But, she said, skepticism persisted in farm country.
"They maintain this position (that) there is a bias... So it made sense" to ask for an outside review.
The Academy of Sciences has a reputation as an unbiased, premiere research group.
Woteki said the new review should not impinge on work in Congress to reauthorize U.S. agricultural research programs. Statutory authority for them expires later this year.
Staff workers on the Senate Agriculture Committee were drafting a bill to renew the programs. The House Agriculture Committee was expected to hold hearings soon on agricultural research.
Glickman told reporters on Tuesday that USDA has provided suggestions to Congress on how to craft an agricultural research bill.
USDA spends more than $1 billion a year on agricultural research through its own network of scientists, universities and other outside research facilities.
